papers.title: The Geometric Function Atlas: Using What We Know About Radius Problems to Solve New Ones
papers.abstract: Usually, radius problems between Ma--Minda classes are solved one pair at a time, by fitting a disk inside the target region, providing a sufficient but not always the sharp radius. The same class appearing under different names makes comparison of results harder, with mistakes and duplication eluding detection. The Geometric Function Atlas catalogs radius problems using exact generators and a direction (source $\to$ target), ensuring unique identification. For each problem, we then compute the radius numerically, together with the point where the image first meets the target boundary. This helps us identify the sharp estimate which guides the proof we write. With this system, we were able to refine two earlier stated estimates, the disk radius for the sine $\to$ modified sigmoid and sine $\to$ rational cases from $\operatorname{arsinh} c$ to $\arcsin c$, and correct earlier stated values for the crescent and exponential classes: the sharp radius is $\sin 1$ from crescent to exponential, and $\log(1+\sqrt2)$ from exponential to crescent. All four proofs follow a common strategy: an estimate that is exact at the contact point, followed by the standard extremal function. Applying the method, we derive fifteen further sharp radii, four of them known.

papers.title: Nef complexity of klt Fano varieties: the full spectrum and classification below two
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a complex klt Fano variety. We study the rational total index $\tau_X$ and the nef complexity $c_X=\dim X+\rho(X)-\tau_X$. Previous joint work of the author with Enwright, Filipazzi, Gongyo, Moraga, Svaldi, and Wang established the corresponding nonnegativity and zero-case characterization in the broader framework of a special class of generalized log Calabi--Yau pairs. Here we give a direct proof in the Fano setting, prove that there is no value strictly between zero and one, and classify all klt Fano varieties with $c_X<2$, without assuming $\mathbb Q$-factoriality. At complexity one, after splitting off projective-space factors, the remaining factor is a normal quadric of Picard number one, a linear blow-up of projective space, or an integral $(1,1)$ hypersurface in a product of projective spaces. If $1<c_X<2$, only two weighted-projective families occur; in particular, no smooth Fano variety has nef complexity strictly between one and two. We also determine the spectrum when the dimension is allowed to vary: \[ \{0\}\cup\left\{2-\frac2q \ \middle| \ q\in\mathbb Z_{\geq2}\right\} \cup(\mathbb Q\cap[2,\infty)). \] Most proofs in this paper were developed from arguments generated by OpenAI's ChatGPT through discussions initiated and guided by the author; see the statement on the use of generative AI.

papers.title: Interior $C^2$ Estimates and a Liouville Theorem for the Complex Monge--Amp\`ere Equation
papers.abstract: We establish an interior $C^2$ estimate for locally bounded plurisubharmonic Bedford-Taylor solutions of the complex Monge--Amp\`ere equation $\det(u_{i\bar j})=f$ under weak quadratic growth bounds on sufficiently large balls, where $f$ is positive and Dini-continuous. We assume a distributional lower bound for the Laplacian of $f^{1/n}$. The main ingredient is a pseudo-$C^2$ estimate using the Green-function averaging error, valid also when $f$ is nonnegative. As an application, we prove that every entire Bedford-Taylor solution of $\det(u_{i\bar j})=1$ with weak quadratic growth is a real quadratic polynomial, resolving a conjecture of G\'abor Sz\'ekelyhidi.

papers.title: Hypercomplex Method for Solving Nonlinear PDEs
papers.abstract: A hypercomplex method for constructing solutions of a class of nonlinear partial differential equations is developed. A family of two-dimensional commutative associative algebras is introduced in which the structural coefficients depend on a component of the monogenic function itself. A corresponding theory of monogenic functions is developed, and nonlinear analogues of the Cauchy-Riemann conditions are obtained. It is shown that the first component of a monogenic function satisfies a broad class of second-order nonlinear partial differential equations whose coefficients depend on the unknown function. A hodograph transformation is used to linearize the nonlinear Cauchy-Riemann system. As a result, the problem of constructing solutions of the nonlinear equations is reduced to solving a second-order linear partial differential equation with variable coefficients, followed by the inverse hodograph transformation. A local correspondence between solutions of the nonlinear Cauchy-Riemann system and solutions of the associated linear equation is established, yielding a constructive algorithm for generating solutions of the original nonlinear PDEs. Several examples are presented in which explicit and implicit solutions of nonlinear second-order PDEs are obtained by this method.

papers.title: Upper Bounds on the de Bruijn-Newman constant for Dirichlet $L$-functions with primitive real-valued characters
papers.abstract: Let $\chi_m$ be a primitive real-valued Dirichlet character of conductor $m\ge3$, let $L(s)=L(s,\chi_m)$ be the associated Dirichlet $L$-function, and let $\xi_L(s)$ denote its completed form. For each $t \in \mathbb R,$ we define the entire function \[ H^L_t(z) := \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} e^{tu^2}\, \Phi_L(u)\, e^{izu}\, du, \] where $\Phi_L$ is the superexponentially decaying density \[ \Phi_L(u) := \frac{1}{2\pi}\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} \xi_L\!\left(\frac{1+is}{2}\right) e^{-isu}\, ds. \] The family $\{H_t^L\}_{t \in \mathbb R}$ describes the heat-flow evolution of $\xi_L$ and solves a backward heat equation. By the work of Newman, there exists a finite constant $\Lambda_L$, called the generalized de Bruijn--Newman constant, such that all the zeros of $H_t^L$ are real if and only if $t \ge \Lambda_L$. The Generalized Riemann Hypothesis (GRH) for $L$ is equivalent to the assertion that $\Lambda_L \le 0$. Dobner established the matching lower bound $\Lambda_L \ge 0$, while de Bruijn proved the upper bound $\Lambda_L \le \tfrac12$. We prove the unconditional uniform bound $\Lambda_L\le953/3200=0.2978125$ for every primitive real-valued character of conductor $3\le m\le400$, together with stronger individual bounds. The proof extends the effective approximation of Polymath to Dirichlet $L$-functions, retaining the conductor dependence in the error estimates. We combine these estimates with Platt's numerical verification of GRH by Platt and rigorous interval computations. We also give conditional bounds under explicit global initial zero-strip hypotheses, including $|\operatorname{Im}z|\le3/4$ for the zeros of $H_0^L$.

papers.title: A new class of smooth algebraic varieties with the density property and a counterexample to the T\'{o}th-Varolin Conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove that the smooth affine hypersurfaces \[ X_{m,n}=\{\zeta^mz_0^n+ (1+z_1\zeta)z_2+\zeta z_3^2=1\}\subset\mathbb{C}^5,\;\; m,n\geq 2, \] have the density property. For every odd integer $d\geq 3$, we identify $X_{d-1,d}$ with a Kaliman modification along a Brieskorn variety of type $(d,2,2,2)$. We prove that the fourfolds $X_{d-1,d}$ are diffeomorphic to $\mathbb{C}^4$ but not biholomorphic to $\mathbb{C}^4$. These, therefore, give counterexamples to the T\'{o}th-Varolin conjecture.

papers.title: The Great Picard theorem for quasiregular values
papers.abstract: We prove a version of Rickman's Great Picard theorem in the theory of quasiregular values. The version of the theorem that we prove is in fact stated in terms of omitted quasiregular values, unlike the previously known Little Picard theorem of the theory that is based on quasiregular values in the boundary of the image set. As a byproduct of the proof, we also prove a Riemann removability theorem in our setting, which ends up strengthening the conclusion of the previously resolved question of Astala, Iwaniec and Martin.

papers.title: Singular solutions to the complex Monge-Amp\`ere equation II
papers.abstract: Continuing our work in [Math. Ann. 392 (2025), 1503-1518], we construct new singular solutions to the complex Monge-Amp\`ere equation with constant right-hand side in the Bedford-Taylor sense. Let $\mathbb D$ denote the open unit disk in $\mathbb C$. For $n\geq 2$, these solutions include: (i) a bounded solution on $\mathbb D^n$ that is discontinuous almost everywhere and nowhere classically differentiable; (ii) a continuous exhaustion of $\mathbb C^n$ that does not belong to $W^{2,1}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb C^n)$; (iii) a continuous solution on $\overline{\mathbb D^n}$ whose Laplacian has a singular part. We construct these solutions from singular harmonic functions using partial Legendre transforms and holomorphic pullbacks.

papers.title: On some connections between Kobayashi geometry and pluripotential theory
papers.abstract: In this paper, we explore some connections between Kobayashi geometry and the Dirichlet problem for the complex Monge--Amp\`ere equation. Among the results we obtain through these connections are: $(i)$~a theorem on the continuous extension up to $\partial{D}$ of a proper holomorphic map $F: D\longrightarrow \Omega$ between domains with $\dim_{\mathbb{C}}(D) < \dim_{\mathbb{C}}(\Omega)$, and $(ii)$~a result that establishes the existence of bounded domains with ``nice'' boundary geometry on which H\"older regularity of the solutions to the complex Monge--Amp\`ere equation fails. The first, a result in Kobayashi geometry, relies upon an auxiliary construction that involves solving the complex Monge--Amp\`ere equation with H\"older estimates. The second result relies crucially on a bound for the Kobayashi metric.

papers.title: Properties of Holomorphic $p$-Contact Manifolds
papers.abstract: We continue the study of compact holomorphic $p$-contact manifolds $X$ that we introduced recently by expanding the discussion to include non-K\"ahler hyperbolicity issues and a differential calculus based on what we call the Lie derivative with respect to a $(0,\,q)$-form with values in the holomorphic tangent bundle of $X$. We also propose the notion of $p$-contact deformations for which we prove a Bogomolov-Tian-Todorov-type unobstructedness theorem to order two. This kind of small deformations of the complex structure is related to the essential horizontal deformations that we introduced in our previous work and forms part of a wider on-going project aimed at developing a non-K\"ahler mirror symmetry theory that was first tested on the Iwasawa manifold and subsequently on Calabi-Yau page-$1$-$\partial\bar\partial$-manifolds.

papers.title: A note on the hypercomplex singular Cauchy-like integral in Douglis analysis
papers.abstract: Hypercomplex analysis extends classical complex analysis to Douglis algebras, replacing holomorphic functions with hyperanalytic functions, i.e., null solutions of the Douglis operator in $\mathbb R^2$ (identifying $\mathbb R^2$ with $\mathbb C$). The hypercomplex singular Cauchy-like integral, is one of the main actors in the hypercomplex analysis and many properties have been studied in recently decades. This paper aims to present local estimates of the hypercomplex singular Cauchy-like integral.

papers.title: From the Optimal $L^2$-Estimates \((p,n)\) and \((n,p)\)-Forms to Uniform Griffiths \(p\)-Positivity via Convolution and Restriction
papers.abstract: We prove that the optimal \(L^2\)-estimate property for \((p,n)\)-forms is preserved under standard convolution regularization. As an application, we show that a singular Hermitian metric satisfying the optimal \(L^2\)-estimate property for \((p,n)\)-forms is uniform Griffiths \(p\)-positive. By establishing the restriction property, we prove that a singular Hermitian metric satisfying the optimal \(L^2\)-estimate property for \((n,p)\)-forms is also uniform Griffiths \(p\)-positive.

papers.title: Foliations and Laminar Currents for $C^2$ Maximal Plurisubharmonic Functions
papers.abstract: Let $u\in C^2(\Omega)\cap\mathrm{PSH}(\Omega)$ satisfy $(dd^c u)^2=0$ on a domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb{C}^2$. We prove that the positive-rank locus of its Levi form carries a foliation by holomorphic curves tangent to the Levi-null directions, along which $u$ is harmonic. The flow boxes are locally bi-Lipschitz; in particular, the Levi-null slope is locally Lipschitz in the transverse variable. The Levi current is uniformly laminar on the positive-rank locus, with an explicit transverse measure, and laminar on $\Omega$. A smooth example also shows that the Levi current can be laminar without being uniformly laminar on the whole domain. The analytic construction combines a local partial Legendre transform with a Hardy-space boundary equation.

papers.title: Global $L^2$ Approximation in the Bergman Spaces with Values in Holomorphic Vector Bundles
papers.abstract: In this paper, we get global $L^2$ approximation theorems in Bergman spaces with values in singular holomorphic vector bundles over Stein manifolds generalizing results of Li and Zhou. The main results combine strong openness property of multiplier submodule sheaf and twisted $L^2$ estimates of $\bar\partial$-equations.

papers.title: Transversality at Virtual Centers
papers.abstract: We consider the family of transcendental meromorphic functions with finitely many singular values, none of whose asymptotic values is infinity. We prove that transversality holds at any boundary point of a shell component in a dynamically natural slice of the parameter space at which an asymptotic value is a prepole.

papers.title: Measures of maximal entropy for meromorphic maps on compact K\"ahler manifolds
papers.abstract: Let $f$ be a dominant meromorphic self-map of a compact K\"ahler manifold. Assume that $f$ has a strictly dominant intermediate dynamical degree $\lambda$ and that the number of isolated $n$-periodic points, counted with multiplicity, is at most $\lambda^n+o(\lambda^n)$. Then $f$ admits at most one adapted invariant probability measure of entropy $\log\lambda$. If such a measure exists, its natural extension is Bernoulli, and the isolated periodic points equidistribute towards it when counted with or without multiplicity. We apply this criterion to several classes of maps in complex dynamics, resolving longstanding open problems.

papers.title: Hurwitz existence problem and fiber products
papers.abstract: With each holomorphic map $f:R\to\mathbb C\mathbb P^1$, where $R$ is a compact Riemann surface, one can associate a combinatorial datum consisting of the genus $g$ of $R$, the degree $n$ of $f$, the number $r$ of critical values of $f$, and the $r$ partitions of $n$ given by the local degrees of $f$ over these critical values. These quantities are related by the Riemann-Hurwitz formula, and the Hurwitz existence problem asks whether a combinatorial datum that fits this formula actually corresponds to some map $f$. In this paper, we use fiber products of holomorphic maps between compact Riemann surfaces to establish general criteria for the non-realizability of branch data. We also deduce from our results the theorem of Halphen, proven in 1880, concerning polynomial solutions of the equation $A(z)^a+B(z)^b=C(z)^c$, where $a,b,c$ are integers greater than one.

papers.title: Equisingularity in families of double point curves
papers.abstract: In this paper, we provide a systematic comparison between the equisingularity of a 1-parameter unfolding $F = (f_t, t)$ of a finitely determined map germ $f: (\mathbb{C}^2, 0) \to (\mathbb{C}^3, 0)$ and the equisingularity of its associated families of double point curves: $D(F)$, $F(D(F))$, $D^2(F)$, and $D^2(F)/S_2$. We also construct explicit counterexamples to several natural questions concerning the equisingularity of these loci. As a key application, we introduce new families of complete intersection curves -- referred to as Henry--type families -- which are topologically trivial but fail to satisfy the Whitney equisingularity conditions. Finally, we generalize classical formulas for double point curves, originally established for map germs from $(\mathbb{C}^2, 0)$ to $(\mathbb{C}^3, 0)$, to the higher-dimensional setting of map germs from $(\mathbb{C}^n, 0)$ to $(\mathbb{C}^{2n-1}, 0)$ for $n \geq 3$, thereby endowing the associated curves with a convenient analytic structure.

papers.title: A solution to the Yau-Tian-Donaldson Conjecture through Special Fujita Approximations
papers.abstract: We show that any big line bundle on a smooth projective variety admits a special Fujita approximation: the volume and the first Riemann-Roch coefficient are both approximated by those of ample $\mathbb{Q}$-line bundles on higher models. Exploiting previous works by Boucksom, Jonsson and Li, we solve the Boucksom-Jonsson Regularization Conjecture on the Non-Archimedean entropy functional. As a main consequence, we obtain a solution to the (uniform version of the) Yau-Tian-Donaldson Conjecture: a polarized smooth projective variety $(X,L)$ admits a cscK metric if and only if it is $\mathrm{Aut}^\circ(X,L)$-uniformly $K$-stable. This extends the known Yau-Tian-Donaldson correspondence for smooth Fano varieties.

papers.title: Failure of local extension of semipositive metrics in a smooth projective family
papers.abstract: We construct a smooth projective family of rational surfaces and an effective line bundle on its total space that give a negative answer to P\u{a}un's metric-extension question. The restricted bundle on the central fibre carries a semipositively curved singular Hermitian metric with analytic and minimal singularities, but this metric admits no semipositive extension to any neighbourhood of the whole fibre, even up to singularity type. The construction uses four-point blow-ups of the plane, with three centres becoming collinear on the central fibre. This change produces a nonzero integrable adjoint section on the central fibre, whereas the corresponding adjoint systems vanish on nearby noncentral fibres. If a metric extension existed, an $L^2$ extension theorem would extend that section, contradicting this vanishing.

papers.title: Paired kernels and truncated Toeplitz operators
papers.abstract: This paper considers paired operators in the context of the Lebesgue Hilbert space $L^2$ on the unit circle and its subspace, the Hardy space $H^2$. The kernels of such operators, together with their analytic projections, which are generalizations of Toeplitz kernels, are studied. Inclusion relations between such kernels are considered in detail, and the results are applied to describing the kernels of finite-rank asymmetric truncated Toeplitz operators.

papers.title: Fractional Besov-Sobolev Spaces on Chord-arc Curves
papers.abstract: Let $\Gamma$ be a bounded rectifiable Jordan curve, with complementary domains $\Omega_i$ and $\Omega_e$. For $1<p<\infty$ and $0<s<1$, we study the spaces $\mathcal B_{p,p}^s(\Omega)$ of harmonic functions satisfying \[ \iint_\Omega |\nabla u(z)|^p \operatorname{dist}(z,\Gamma)^{(1-s)p-1}\,dA(z)<\infty, \qquad \Omega\in\{\Omega_i,\Omega_e\}. \] When $\Gamma$ is the unit circle, these two spaces coincide with a fractional Besov-Sobolev space $B^s_{p,p}(\Gamma)$. The equivalence of boundary seminorms and harmonic energies on the circle raises a geometric question: which rough curves preserve these estimates? For every radial-Lipschitz curve $\Gamma$, we prove \[ \operatorname{Tr}_\Gamma\mathcal B_{p,p}^s(\Omega_i) =B_{p,p}^s(\Gamma) =\operatorname{Tr}_\Gamma\mathcal B_{p,p}^s(\Omega_e) \] whenever either $1 < p \le 2$ and $2/p - 1 < s < 1$, or $2 < p < \infty$ and $0 < s < 1/2 + 1/p$. For arbitrary chord-arc curves, the same trace identities hold when $1/p\le s<1/2+1/(2p)$. Taking $s=1-1/p$ yields an almost-Dirichlet principle for the unweighted $p$-energy on radial-Lipschitz domains when $3/2<p<4$, and on chord-arc domains when $2\le p<3$. For every $p>4$, this principle fails on a suitable radial-Lipschitz domain, showing that the upper bound $4$ cannot be increased uniformly over this class.

papers.title: Separation properties of a hybrid point process with determinantal radii and uniform arguments
papers.abstract: We recently characterized the almost sure separation of determinantal point processes $\Lambda_\phi$ in the plane associated with Fock spaces $\mathcal F_\phi$ with doubling weights $\phi$. We also showed that, as expected, a more restrictive condition is required to characterize the almost surely separated Poisson processes with the same first intensity as $\Lambda_\phi$. To gain further insight into this difference in behavior, we focus on radial weights $\phi$ and introduce a hybrid process $\Lambda_\phi^M=\{r_j e^{i\theta_j}\}_{j}$, where the moduli $r_j$ are taken from $\Lambda_\phi$, while the arguments $\theta_j$ are chosen independently and uniformly in $[0,2\pi)$, independently of the radii. Our main result is that the hybrid process is almost surely separated under exactly the same condition as the corresponding Poisson process. Thus, despite preserving the joint radial distribution of the determinantal process, independent angular randomization destroys its improved separation properties.

papers.title: Normality Criteria for Quasimeromorphic Mappings: Avoidance and Sharing
papers.abstract: We establish normality criteria for families of quasimeromorphic mappings in \(\mathbb{R}^n\), \(n\geq 2\), based on the avoidance and sharing of continuous functions. We first establish a rescaling principle for sequences of continuous functions and use it to derive a higher-dimensional analogue of Lappan's avoidance criterion. We then obtain normality criteria based on the sharing of continuous functions. In particular, we prove that a family of \(K\)-quasimeromorphic mappings sharing \(q_0(n,K)+1\) mutually disjoint continuous functions is normal, where \(q_0(n,K)\) is the corresponding quasiregular Picard constant. We further consider sequences of quasimeromorphic mappings sharing sequences of continuous functions with a normal comparison sequence and establish a corresponding normality criterion, together with an improved bound under an additional separation condition on the limiting functions. Finally, we derive applications to normal quasiregular mappings into \(\mathbb{S}^n\).

papers.title: A problem for isolated singularities of surfaces
papers.abstract: Let $E\subset\mathbf R^n$ be a set of dimension $2$ with an isolated singular point $0$, such that $E-\{0\}$ is an orientable $\mathcal C^2$ submanifold of $\mathbf R^n$ of dimension $2$, and hence a Riemann surface with the conformal structure induced by the ambient metric. We study the extension of its conformal structure across $0$, under hypotheses that are metric rather than analytic. The main result (1989) is that the isolated singularity $0$ is $\mathit{conformally \ point-like}$ (conformal to a punctured disc) whenever it is $\mathit{$M$-regular}$ : the pair $(E-\{0\},\{0\})$ satisfies a Whitney condition, and the length of the spherical slice $S(0,r)\cap E$ (a curve), where $S(0,r)$ is the sphere of radius $r$ centred at $0$, is bounded above by a linear function of $r$, a condition described as ''metric decay''. This is proven using an argument based on the modulus of rings (extremal length), which generalizes the classical planar technique to $2$-dimensional submanifolds of $\mathbb{R}^n$. Two classes of examples are examined: surfaces of revolution generated by a 1-dimensional curve and subanalytic sets of dimension 2 ---for which $M$-regularity is proven directly from Hironaka's structure theory---leading to the corollary that every isolated singularity of a $2$-dimensional orientable subanalytic set is conformally point-like. In this case the metric decay condition is obtained from a direct estimate of the volume of the slices $S(0,r)\cap E$ (Lemma 7.5), based on Hironaka's Whitney theorem and Stasica's decomposition into $L$-analytic pieces. A further original result is a $C^\infty$ counterexample showing that a strict Whitney condition alone does $\mathit{not}$ imply the linear length bound: the two hypotheses in the definition of $M$-regularity are independent.
